title: Privileged mintFor()/burn() ignore global paused + per-index disabled flags
rootCauseClass: incomplete pause/disabled enforcement on privileged supply-changing entry points
fingerprintBasis: src/V2/NFTMinterV2.sol:mintFor/burn:incomplete pause/disabled enforcement on privileged supply-changing entry points
description: The privileged supply-changing entry points mintFor() (lines 206-214) and burn() (lines 341-345) do not re-apply the global paused guard nor the per-index configs[index].disabled guard that the permissionless _executeMint path enforces. When the owner sets configs[index].disabled = true (documented as 'new mints are blocked') or the contract is paused, the trusted migrator can still mint/burn that index. The pause-exempt leg is deliberate-by-design (a pause-exempt migration primitive justified by the reverted story-033), so that leg is faithful; the residual defect is the disabled-bypass, a Law-2 spec deviation from the documented 'new mints are blocked' semantics with no authorizing story.
impact: No asset theft or net inflation: mintFor() mints exactly 1 claim NFT 1:1 against a burned V1 NFT and is gated to authorizedMinters (only the trusted NFTMigrator is wired); burn() is gated to authorizedBurners. The defect is a kill-switch completeness gap (incorrect state-handling / spec-conformance), not an asset path. A non-obvious owner footgun: an owner who disables an index would be surprised the migrator path can still mint it.
attackPath: Not externally attacker-executable: both entry points require authorizedMinters[msg.sender] / authorizedBurners[msg.sender], which only the trusted migrator holds.
Operator sets configs[index].disabled = true intending 'new mints blocked', or the pauser pauses the contract.
The trusted migrator calls mintFor(index, recipient); _executeMint's !paused / !disabled guards are absent on mintFor, so the mint proceeds anyway.
Result: the disabled/paused index is still mintable via the privileged path, contradicting documented semantics — but only the trusted minter benefits and supply stays 1:1 vs burned V1.
recommendation: Re-apply the per-index disabled check (and, if pause-exemption is not actually required for migration, the paused check) on mintFor()/burn(), or explicitly document the privileged path as disabled/pause-exempt so the 'new mints are blocked' semantics are not silently violated.
corroboratingSources: findings/story-faithfulness.json: F-03 disabled-bypass spec deviation (documented 'new mints blocked')
